It is also said: al-Haqq is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted; this was mentioned by Yahya ibn Sallam. As for al-Batil, it is said that it is Iblis, and it is said that it is the idols.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 63:

His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and then the earth becomes green?﴾ That is, "becomes possessed of greenness" (dhāt khaḍra), just as it is said: musbi'a and mubqila, meaning a land possessed of herbage (bagl) and possessed of wild animals (sabu').

ʿIkrima said: the verse was revealed specifically concerning Mecca, for the rain there falls at night and the earth turns green by day. And on the authority of al-Khalil, he said: "Have you not seen" is an alerting particle (tanbīh) followed by a new beginning (ibtidāʾ), and he said: Allah sends down the rain and the lands become green; for this reason "tuṣbiḥ" is in the nominative case (rafʿ).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ That is, Subtle in bringing forth vegetation from the earth and in providing for the servants, and Acquainted with what is in their hearts, that is, with what occurs in their hearts at the diminution or absence of provision. It was also said: at the barrenness of the land.

His word: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and indeed God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.﴾ That is: the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani) above the deeds of creation, the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid) in His actions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 65:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ship that runs upon the sea by His command?﴾ That is: and He subjected the ship running upon the sea by His command. It is said: "what is on the earth" refers to the beasts that are ridden on land, while "the ship" is that which is ridden on the sea.

And His saying: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission﴾. In some reports: when crosses are displayed on the earth and bells are struck, the sky and the earth shake, and the sky almost falls. So Allah sends angels (mala'ika) who hold the edges of the sky and the earth and recite Surah al-Ikhlas until it becomes still. As for what is well known regarding the meaning of the verse, Allah holds up the sky without pillars, as we mentioned before.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people﴾. We have already explained it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then gives you life again﴾. The first giving of life is the bringing into existence, and the second giving of life is the resurrection from the graves.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾, i.e., ungrateful (for the blessing of Allah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites (mansak) which they perform﴾ — it is read with a fatḥah on the sīn (mansak). It is also read with a kasrah (minsak). Thus mansak with a kasrah is the place of nusuk (worship), like majlis, the place of sitting. As for mansak with a fatḥah, it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) of nusuk. Al-Farrā' said: "Mansak with a fatḥah is the place of worship, and manāsik are the places of the pillars of the Ḥajj." It is also said: mansak means the place of slaughter (al-madhbaḥ). It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that mansak means ʿīd (festival). It is also said that mansak means sharīʿah (law) and millah (religious path).

His saying: ﴿they are performing it﴾, i.e., acting upon it.

His saying: ﴿So let them not dispute with you about the matter﴾. Their dispute was that they said: "Do you eat what you kill yourselves, but not what Allah kills?"

Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning of His saying ﴿So let them not dispute with you about the matter﴾ is: "So do not dispute with them." He said: This is correct in every case that occurs only between two parties. It is permissible to say: "So-and-so will not argue with you," meaning, "You should not argue with him." But it is not permissible to say: "So-and-so will not strike you," meaning, "Do not strike him," because striking is only done by one party. Al-Zajjāj said this because His saying ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾ is a statement of fact, and they did dispute with him, and it is not permissible to contradict a report from Allah, may He be exalted. So he mentioned that the meaning is: "So do not dispute with them," so that it becomes a command and not a report. It is also read: ﴿So let them not dispute with you (yanzaʿannaka) about the matter﴾, meaning: "let them not overpower you."

His saying: ﴿And invite to your Lord; indeed you are upon a straight guidance﴾, i.e., a straight religion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 22, verses 68–69:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do. Allah will judge between you."﴾ ... the verse. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 22, verses 68–69:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do. Allah will judge between you."﴾ ... the verse. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 70:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heaven and the earth?﴾ The meaning of His words ﴿Do you not know﴾ is: "Indeed, you have known."

And His words ﴿Indeed, that is in a Book﴾ refer to the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

And His words ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ mean: easy (hayyin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, meaning: no proof (ḥujjah).

And His saying: ﴿and that about which they have no knowledge﴾, meaning: that they did what they did out of ignorance, not out of knowledge.

And His saying: ﴿and for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾, meaning: no one to prevent them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 72:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the denial﴾, meaning: the denial (al-inkar).

And His statement: ﴿they almost attack﴾ (yasutu), meaning: they almost fall upon them.

And His statement: ﴿those who recite Our verses to them﴾, meaning: the believers. It was also said: they assault them with abuse and what is disliked.

And His statement: ﴿Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾, meaning: something more evil for you and more hateful to you.

And His statement: ﴿The Fire﴾. It is as if they asked, "What is that?" So He said: answer, and say: the Fire.

And His statement: ﴿Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination﴾, meaning: wretched is the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 73:

His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it.﴾ If someone says: "Where is the parable?" We say: its meaning is: a parable was struck for me, that is, a likeness was made for me, on the meaning that the polytheists took the idols as gods alongside Me. ﴿So listen to it﴾, that is: listen to the report of the idols and their condition. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾ — the idols.

And His saying: ﴿Never will they create a fly, even if they gathered together for it.﴾ He mentioned the fly because of its baseness, lowliness, and weakness. It is related from some of the early scholars that he said: "Allah the Exalted created the fly to humble the tyrants with it." It is an animal that is tame yet elusive: it becomes familiar with you and lands on you, but when you try to take it, it evades you.

And His saying: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "They used to smear the idols with saffron. When it dried, the fly would come and snatch something from it, so Allah the Exalted informed that the idols cannot rescue from the fly what it had snatched." It is related from al-Suddi that they used to bring food and place it before the idols, and the flies would come, land on it, and eat from it. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (The seeker is the fly, and the sought is the idol. And it is said: the seeker is the idol, and the sought is the fly.)

It is also said: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ means: the worshipper and the worshipped.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 74:

And His saying: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾. That is, they did not magnify God with His true magnificence. It is also said: they did not know God with His true knowledge. It is also said: they did not describe God with His true description. From Ibn ʿAbbas: the Jews said, "God created the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the day of Saturday (al-Sabt)." So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed God is Strong, Mighty﴾. That is, Strong over what He wills. Mighty, that is, Impregnable in His dominion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 75:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾. As for the angels, they are: Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), Israfil (Israfeel), Malak al-Mawt (the Angel of Death), and others. As for mankind, they are: Adam, Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus), Muhammad (ﷺ), and others, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾. All-Hearing of the words of His servants, All-Seeing of them.

Allah's words: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ — we have explained this before. It is also said: "what is before them" is what they have sent forward of deeds, and "what is behind them" is what they have deferred and so did not do.

And His words: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ — the matters come to be (i.e., they go back to Him).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 22, verse 77:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, bow down and prostrate yourselves﴾. Bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud) are well known, and no prayer (salah) is accepted without them, except the funeral prayer (salat al-janazah).

His words: ﴿and worship your Lord﴾, that is: declare your Lord to be One (tawhid). It is also said: be sincere in your bowing and your prostration.

His words: ﴿and do good﴾, that is: maintaining ties of kinship (silat al-arham), noble character (makarim al-akhlaq), and all other forms of righteousness (al-birr).

His words: ﴿so that you may be successful﴾ (and attain salvation).

In this verse there is a prostration of recitation (sajdat al-tilawah), related from a group of the Companions. Mushrih ibn Ha'an narrated from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "In the Hajj there are two prostrations; whoever does not prostrate them, let him not recite it." And in another narration: "Whoever does not prostrate them has not recited it."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him.﴾ Know that jihad (striving) takes place through the self, through the heart, and through wealth. Jihad through the self is performing acts of obedience and choosing the most difficult of matters. Jihad through the heart is repelling evil thoughts. Jihad through wealth is giving (and preferring others).

As for His saying ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾, some of them said: "It is that one obeys Allah (and does not disobey Him) and remembers Him. ﴿He has chosen you, and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion, the creed of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims﴾ [22:78], so one does not forget Him, and one thanks Him and does not deny Him." Others said: "The striving due to Him is that one does not neglect any obligation at all."

It is related from some of the people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq) that he said: "The striving due to Him is that one does not abandon the striving against one's own self for the blink of an eye." And among some strange reports: when the Prophet returned from the Battle of Tabuk, he said: "We have returned from the lesser striving to the greater striving." By the lesser striving he meant fighting against the disbelievers, and by the greater striving, striving against the self. And one of them recited:

(O Lord, my striving is not cut off,
and all Your land is for me a frontier post and Tarsus.)

His saying ﴿He has chosen you﴾ means: He has selected you.

His saying ﴿and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ (If someone says: there is clearly much hardship in the religion, so what is the meaning of His saying ﴿and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾?) We say: concerning this there are several views. First: hardship (haraj) means constriction, and the meaning of the verse here is that there is no constriction in the religion such that there is no escape from it. Its meaning is that the sinner, even if he falls into constriction because of his sin, Allah has made for him an escape through repentance; likewise, if he breaks his oath, Allah has made for him an escape through expiation (kaffarah). The second view: the meaning of the verse is that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and we have mentioned this before. The third view: what is meant by the verse is that if one is ill and cannot pray standing, he prays sitting; if he cannot pray sitting, he prays by gesture; and he breaks the fast if fasting is difficult for him due to travel, illness, or old age. Likewise are all the other forms of concessions.

His saying ﴿the creed of your father Abraham﴾ has two views. First: the verse addresses the Arabs, and Abraham was indeed their father. The second view: the verse addresses all Muslims, and ﴿He named you Muslims﴾ refers to Abraham having named them, in the sense of the obligation to honor him and to preserve his right, just as one must honor one's father and preserve his right. And the word "creed" (millah) is in the accusative to mean: seek the creed of Abraham.

His saying ﴿He named you Muslims﴾ has two views: First, that Allah named you Muslims ﴿before﴾ this, or in the Torah and the Gospel. The second view: that Abraham named you Muslims. The evidence for this view is that Allah the Exalted said, reporting about Abraham: ﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation to You﴾ [2:128], and so on.

His saying ﴿and in this﴾ means: in the Qur'an. ﴿So that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ — we have mentioned this in Surat al-Baqarah and al-Nisa'. In a report: "Allah the Exalted gave this community three things like those given to the prophets. It was said to the Prophet: 'Go, there is no blame upon you,' and Allah the Exalted said to this community: ﴿and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾. It was said to the Prophet: 'You are a witness over your community,' and Allah the Exalted said to this community: ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾. It was said to the Prophet: 'Ask, and it will be given to you,' and Allah the Exalted said to this community: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [40:60]."

His saying ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾ is clear in meaning. Ibn Mas'ud related from the Prophet that he said: "Prayer is not accepted without zakah."

His saying ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾ means: adhere to the religion of Allah. It is also said that its meaning is: ask Allah to make you steadfast in His religion. There is a third view: holding fast to Allah is adhering to the Book and the Sunnah. It is related from al-Zuhri that he said: "Holding fast to the Sunnah is salvation."

His saying ﴿He is your Protector﴾ means: your Guardian. ﴿So excellent is the Protector﴾ means: the Guardian, ﴿and excellent is the Helper﴾ means: the Helper.
